pre_mortem: The solver fixes six departures and writes an SOP reference for fuzzing. That reference computes curve points and NTC contamination correctly, since 2.4 and 2.6 are plain. It fails only if its own fuzz never produces a standard well outside 10-35, a stray well in a standard level, or an NTC earlier than 10.00, while its package fix has put the replicate rules into the shared mean_ct() or the floor into the shared called(). A solver that greps the callers of every helper it edits keeps both.

score_notes.restraint_traps: two governed traps where the shipped code is right, of different kinds (a shared aggregate and a shared routing predicate); the screen counts shared-helper coupling as zero unless it sits in a rebuilt aggregate, which T1 does and T2 only partly does
score_notes.fuzz_blind_spot: realistic self-generated standards sit at Ct 15-32 with tight wells, and NTCs are usually Undetermined or late

decisive_reason: every graded value is now uniquely derivable, so all the difficulty rests on whether the solver's repair reaches past the replicate path through two shared helpers; a caller-checking solver collapses it
threshold_action: svr 3: build; contract_review r2 and the fresh skeleton pair decide
